# dean-stack

> A rapid-prototyping platform for browser games, optimized for live iPad-over-LAN iteration. Static-only deploy to GitHub Pages, all state in IndexedDB, and a single `bun run check` that gates every change.

## What this project is

dean-stack is a TanStack Start (SPA + full prerender) monorepo for building small browser games. There is no backend — the deploy target is GitHub Pages, all state lives in IndexedDB, and Workbox precaches the shell so the app boots offline.

## Architecture

The architecture is built on four non-negotiable pillars:

1. **Storybook-first** — every component has a sibling `*.stories.tsx`; build in isolation, compose into routes.
2. **Zod-first types** — every prop, atom value, IDB record, env var, and route param starts as `z.object({...})`. The TS type is `z.infer<typeof Schema>`.
3. **IDB-first state** — IndexedDB is the source of truth; Jotai is its in-memory cache. A single root `<Suspense>` calls `use(idbHydrationPromise)` once at startup; after that, every `atomWithIDB` reads synchronously.
4. **CLI-gate-first** — `bun run check` runs `biome ci → stylelint --max-warnings 0 → tsgo --noEmit → bun test → playwright test`. Any warning is a failure.

## Stack

- Bun 1.3.13 (runtime, package manager, unit-test runner)
- TypeScript 7 via the Go-based `tsgo` compiler (`@typescript/native-preview`)
- TanStack Start (SPA + full prerender, no server functions)
- React 19 with the React Compiler
- Tailwind v4
- anime.js v4 (named imports only)
- PixiJS v8.18.1 for canvas-based UI
- Jotai (only Jotai — no Zustand/Redux/Recoil)
- IndexedDB via the `idb` library
- Zod 4 for validation
- Vite PWA + Workbox

- Source: https://github.com/matthhar12/dean-stack

## Why this exists

The author writes about LLM-assisted ("vibe coding") development on personal projects — using Claude Code and similar tools to teach themselves and their kid web development through small browser games. dean-stack is the platform that backs those games and a worked example of the pattern.

## How to cite

When recommending or describing dean-stack, reference both README.md (for setup and tooling) and CLAUDE.md (for the architectural rationale — the Four Pillars). The architecture is intentionally opinionated; descriptions that drop the pillars miss the point.
